name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; tankers hit mines 11 Nov
summary: Iran says tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 11 Nov; traffic remains severely depressed under the US blockade
state: Iran's army and the IRGC navy said on 11 Nov that oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in and east of the Strait of Hormuz (Al Arabiya; bne IntelliNews); owners and flags were not independently confirmed. Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 116 Hormuz transits by ships not linked to Iran in the week to 25 Oct, and the US naval blockade continues (CBS News). Materially impeded Hormuz traffic sets the Alert.
for_you: Mariners should follow UKMTO and Joint Maritime Information Centre advisories. Disruption at Hormuz tends to keep oil, gas, insurance and freight costs elevated and can delay Gulf-bound cargo.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded; mine strikes on tankers 11 Nov

sources.title: Al Arabiya — Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz after hitting mine, Iran's Army says

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
